name: Dopamine
high_alert_note: Falls within the vasopressors named in the FDA infusion pump page's examples of high-risk infusions; the local high-alert list governs.
summary: Catecholamine used to improve haemodynamic status in distributive shock or shock due to reduced cardiac output. Nursing focus: tissue ischaemia, arrhythmias, abrupt discontinuation and sulfite hypersensitivity.
evidence_type_note: The evidence here is a regulator product label (prescribing information written for prescribers and pharmacists). It is not a bedside nursing practice guideline: the nursing actions are inferences from label warnings, marked partial, and the unit's protocol governs practice.
jurisdiction_note: US FDA label only. EMA, MHRA and SFDA labels were not read; indications, warnings and presentations differ by country and by manufacturer.

items.text: The label describes dopamine as a catecholamine indicated to improve haemodynamic status in patients in distributive shock or shock due to reduced cardiac output.
Check the extremities and the infusion site regularly and report coolness, pallor or leakage; do not stop or interrupt the infusion without an instruction.
Monitoring frequency and alarm limits follow the unit's protocol for this medicine.
The label calls for monitoring of the skin of the extremities in susceptible patients and for monitoring patients who have arrhythmias.
Tissue ischaemia: severe peripheral and visceral vasoconstriction can occur; the label advises addressing hypovolaemia before use, monitoring the extremities and infusing into a large vein.
Cardiac arrhythmias can occur and the patient should be monitored closely.
Hypotension after abrupt discontinuation: the label advises gradually reducing the infusion while expanding blood volume (a prescriber decision).
Severe hypersensitivity due to a sodium metabisulfite excipient may cause anaphylaxis or asthmatic episodes in susceptible people.
The label lists tissue ischaemia, cardiac arrhythmias and hypotension among the adverse reactions described in its warnings.
Escalate for cold or mottled limbs, new arrhythmia, falling blood pressure, an interrupted infusion or allergic signs.
Record the product and order checks, monitoring results, adverse events and escalation per unit standard.
Institution-specific preparation: follow your pharmacy's preparation standard and the product labelling. This library gives no preparation or concentration instructions.
Institution-specific dosing: follow the prescriber's order and your institution's approved protocol. This library gives no dosing instructions.

monitoring.text: Inspect the extremities and infusion site.
Monitor rhythm and blood pressure closely.
Check for sulfite or allergy history.
Report ischaemia signs, arrhythmia or an interrupted infusion immediately.
